blocks.text: How Water Damage Restoration Works in McDonough Homes
Water damage restoration follows six steps: inspect, extract, dry, clean, monitor and repair. Most McDonough homes finish drying in 3 to 5 days.

items: Inspect and map the moisture. The crew confirms the source is stopped, then uses moisture meters and thermal imaging to trace where water went behind walls, under floors and into ceilings. You see the plan before major work begins.
Extract the water. Pumps and extractors pull standing water out of carpet, pad and hard floors. Every gallon removed now saves days of drying.
Remove only what can't be saved. Soaked pad, swollen baseboards or contaminated drywall come out. Everything that can be dried in place stays.
Dry and dehumidify. Air movers pull moisture out of materials while commercial dehumidifiers pull it out of the air. Wall cavities, cabinets and subfloors get targeted drying.
Clean and sanitize. Affected areas are cleaned and treated with antimicrobial products. Sewage and floodwater areas are fully disinfected.
Monitor, then rebuild. Moisture is measured and logged daily until everything is truly dry. Then drywall, flooring, trim and paint go back so the room looks like nothing happened.

blocks.text: A wall can feel dry and still be wet inside. Drying until the readings say so, not until it looks dry, is what prevents hidden mold weeks later.
Why Water Damage Hits McDonough and Henry County Homes
Most water damage in McDonough comes from four local causes: hard freezes, heavy rain, damp crawl spaces and long humid summers.
Hard freezes and burst pipes in Henry County

Georgia pipes often run through attics, garages, exterior walls and vented crawl spaces with little insulation. When hard freezes hit metro Atlanta, as they did at Christmas 2022 and in January 2024, pipes split and flood homes as they thaw. Georgia ranked first in the nation for one major insurer's paid frozen-pipe claims, about $100 million in a single year. See how we handle burst and frozen pipe water damage.
Heavy rain and South River flash flooding

McDonough gets roughly 50 inches of rain a year. Intense storms overwhelm yard drainage and push water under doors, into garages and down into crawl spaces. Flash flood warnings in Henry County have named the South River near downtown McDonough. Our flood and storm damage cleanup treats that water as contaminated from the start.
Wet crawl spaces over Henry County red clay

Many Henry County homes sit over vented crawl spaces. Clay soil holds water, and poor grading or short downspouts send rain straight to the foundation. The signs: standing water below, sagging floors and a musty smell upstairs. Learn more about crawl space water damage and drying.
Georgia humidity and nonstop AC overflows

Air conditioners run for months here. Clogged condensate lines overflow from attic air handlers into ceilings, and humid air keeps wet materials from drying on their own, which is why AC leak water damage so often turns into mold.

Henry County grew past 240,000 people by 2020. Many homes built in the 1990s and 2000s now have water heaters, supply hoses and plumbing at the end of their lifespan, and that shows up as sudden water heater leaks, washing machine and appliance leaks and hidden slab leaks.

Pipe Burst in Your McDonough Home? Do This First

Shut off the main water valve. In most McDonough homes it's where the water line enters the house: the garage, a utility closet, near the water heater or in the crawl space. The curb valve in the meter box at the street also works with a meter key or wrench.

Call a plumber for the pipe and call us for the water damage. Drying shouldn't wait for the plumbing repair.
Why Pipes Freeze and Burst in Henry County Homes

Georgia homes aren't built for long hard freezes. Pipes here often run through unheated attics, garages, exterior walls and vented crawl spaces with little insulation. When temperatures drop into the teens, water in those pipes freezes, expands and splits the pipe, and the leak shows up when it thaws.

It happens more than people expect. Hard freezes at Christmas 2022 and in January 2024 burst pipes in homes and businesses across metro Atlanta, and Georgia ranked first in the nation for one major insurer's paid frozen-pipe claims, about $100 million between August 2022 and August 2023.

items: Supply lines in attics and over garages
Pipes in exterior walls, especially north-facing kitchens and bathrooms
Pipes in vented crawl spaces (see crawl space water damage)
Outdoor hose bibs left connected or uncovered
Plumbing to bonus rooms and additions
